subsystems.name: Micro-robot unit
subsystems.role: the individual agent — a few centimetres or smaller, with just enough sensing, movement and grip to do one simple job.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: a robot too small for a useful battery must scavenge energy locally or be tethered.
parts: small storage capacitor or thin-film cell

subsystems.name: Local communication and positioning
subsystems.role: no satellite navigation exists off-world, so robots must locate themselves relative to neighbours.
parts: ranging from signal strength or timing

subsystems.name: Swarm control layer
subsystems.role: a handful of local rules produce a chosen global shape or task without any central controller.

subsystems.name: Aggregation and structure
subsystems.role: thousands of units must physically bind to push, dig or build as one body.

subsystems.name: Fabrication and deployment
subsystems.role: the economics of terraforming demand millions of identical units made cheaply.

buildSteps.title: Prove the unit
buildSteps.detail: Build a single robot that can move, sense a neighbour and grip another unit reliably.

buildSteps.title: Scale the swarm in the lab
buildSteps.detail: Run hundreds to a few thousand units on a flat arena to show that only local rules are needed for coherent motion, clustering and shape change.

buildSteps.title: Add relative localisation
buildSteps.detail: Develop ranging and dead-reckoning that works with no external positioning, since off-world sites have no navigation satellites.

buildSteps.title: Show physical work
buildSteps.detail: Get a swarm to move regolith, form a load-bearing arch or trench, and recover when units fail.

buildSteps.title: Design for mass production
buildSteps.detail: Strip the unit to parts that can be batch-fabricated at very low cost, accepting short lifetimes.

buildSteps.title: Solve energy and disposal
buildSteps.detail: Decide how millions of units are powered (likely local sunlight) and how they degrade without contaminating the site.

buildSteps.title: Field-trial off-world
buildSteps.detail: Deploy a small swarm on the Moon or Mars to test dust, radiation, temperature swings and communication delay.

buildSteps.title: Scale toward surface modification
buildSteps.detail: Only after those steps could a swarm be considered for large-scale reshaping of terrain — the terraforming premise.

prerequisites.tech: Swarm robotics with thousands of units
prerequisites.why: demonstrated in laboratory arenas, but never in the field at the scale or lifetime a planetary job needs.

prerequisites.tech: Micro-fabrication at very low unit cost
prerequisites.why: the approach only works if units are cheap enough to lose by the million.

prerequisites.tech: Autonomous operation with long communication delay
prerequisites.why: Earth-based control of Mars robots already forces high autonomy; a swarm makes it harder.
solar power on Mars is weaker and dust-prone, and nights are long and cold.

prerequisites.tech: Planetary protection rules and ecology models
prerequisites.why: releasing millions of machines on another body raises contamination questions with no agreed framework.

pathway.milestone: laboratory swarms of hundreds to thousands of simple robots performing collective tasks
pathway.unlocks: algorithms and hardware lessons that scale with unit count, not with complexity.

pathway.milestone: field swarms of a few hundred units on the Moon or Mars doing surveying, digging or assembly
pathway.unlocks: real data on dust, radiation, attrition and repair.

pathway.milestone: self-replicating or self-assembling swarms that build large structures from local material
pathway.unlocks: construction capacity far beyond what a few rovers can deliver.
a possible, unproven route toward terraforming — an idea with no demonstrated pathway yet.
